title: More than a dozen major banks moving forward with stablecoin venture
dek: Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Santander, and others in a consortium of more than a dozen financial institutions are advancing plans for a global stablecoin focused initially on the U.S. dollar. The move reverses years of institutional skepticism about blockchain-based payment tokens.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: A consortium of more than a dozen major banks including Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Santander is advancing plans for a global stablecoin venture initially focused on the U.S. dollar, reversing years of resistance to blockchain-based payment infrastructure.
bottom_line: Watch for announcements naming the full consortium membership and the launch timeline for the stablecoin venture. The narrative holds if major banks formally commit funding and regulatory approval pathways clarify; it breaks if the consortium dissolves or if JPMorgan and other large institutions publicly withdraw support.
body: A consortium of more than a dozen financial institutions including Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Santander is advancing plans for a global stablecoin venture initially focused on the U.S. dollar, according to The Daily Hodl reporting on August 28. The move represents a reversal of the banking sector's historical stance: after years of institutional skepticism about blockchain-based payment tokens, major banks large and small have begun warming to the prospect of issuing their own stablecoins.

Some banking executives had earlier expressed doubts about demand for stablecoin products. That skepticism appears to be softening as competition grows in the payments market and as the stablecoin sector itself has expanded to represent a market worth hundreds of billions of dollars, per the source.

JPMorgan Chase, which already operates JPM Coin (a tokenized deposit system), evaluated whether it could launch its own stablecoin, though a spokeswoman stated the bank has no current plans to issue one. The discussions remain preliminary, according to reporting, though she added the bank could evaluate options depending on customer demand and the regulatory environment.

Separately, a consortium of 39 state bankers associations representing roughly 3,000 banks announced plans for a bank-owned blockchain platform, per The Daily Hodl. The source does not specify which additional banks beyond Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Santander comprise the dozen-plus institution consortium, nor does it detail the timeline for launch, regulatory framework required, design mechanics, or whether the venture would operate as a single platform or as separate bank-branded tokens.
